{{Short description|Transported package of a diplomatic mission, exempt from inspection or seizure}}
[[File:Swedish-diplomatic-pouch.jpg|thumb|A [[Sweden|Swedish]] diplomatic pouch|alt=Refer to caption]]
A '''diplomatic bag''', also known as a '''diplomatic pouch''', is a container with certain legal protections used for carrying official correspondence or other items between a [[diplomatic mission]] and its home government or other diplomatic, consular, or otherwise official entity.<ref name="Boczek">{{cite book
  | last = Boczek
  | first = Boleslaw Adam
  | title = International Law: A Dictionary
  | publisher = Scarecrow Press
  | year = 2005
  | pages = 51–52
  | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=NR7mFXCB-wgC&q=%22diplomatic+bag%22+definition&pg=PA51
  | isbn = 0-8108-5078-8
  | access-date = 2020-11-05
  | archive-date = 2021-11-13
  | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20211113174003/https://books.google.com/books?id=NR7mFXCB-wgC&q=%22diplomatic+bag%22+definition&pg=PA51
  | url-status = live
  }}</ref> The physical concept of a "diplomatic bag" is flexible and it can take many forms (e.g., a [[cardboard box]], [[briefcase]], [[duffel bag]], large [[suitcase]], [[crate]] or even a [[shipping container]]).<ref name="Boczek" />

Additionally, a diplomatic bag usually has some form of lock or [[tamper-evident]] seal attached to it to deter or detect interference by unauthorized third parties. The most important point is that as long as it is externally marked to show its status, the container has [[diplomatic immunity]] from search or seizure,<ref name=BBC>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/672786.stm |title=Diplomatic bag: The inside story |work=BBC News |date=March 10, 2000 |access-date=2008-10-05 |archive-date=2007-03-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070317172223/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/672786.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> as codified in article 27 of the 1961 [[Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations]].<ref name=UN>{{cite web |url=http://legal.un.org/ilc/texts/instruments/english/conventions/9_1_1961.pdf |title=Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations 1961 |publisher=United Nations |access-date=2008-10-05 |archive-date=2019-11-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191111183208/http://legal.un.org/ilc/texts/instruments/english/conventions/9_1_1961.pdf |url-status=live }}, p. 8</ref> It may only contain articles intended for official use,<ref name=UN/> though there have been numerous cases where the privileges of the diplomatic bag have been used to facilitate [[smuggling]]. Bags are often escorted by a [[diplomatic courier]], who is similarly immune from arrest and detention.<ref name=BBC/><ref name=UN/>
[[File:Chinese Diplomatic Bag.jpg|thumb|A [[People's Republic of China|Chinese]] diplomatic bag|alt=Refer to caption]]

==Noteworthy shipments==
* During [[World War II]], [[Winston Churchill]] reportedly received shipments of [[Cuban cigar]]s by this method.<ref name=BBC/>
* [[Triplex (espionage)|Triplex]] was a British espionage operation in [[World War II]] which involved secretly copying the contents of diplomatic pouches of neutral countries.
* In 1964, a Moroccan-born [[Israel]]i double agent named [[Mordechai Louk]] was drugged, bound, and placed in a diplomatic mailing crate at the [[Egypt]]ian Embassy in [[Rome]], but was rescued by Italian authorities.<ref name="NYT expels">{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |title=Italy Expels 2 Egyptian Envoys Accused in Trunk Abduction Attempt |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1964/11/19/archives/italy-expels-2-egyptian-envoys-accused-in-trunk-abduction-attempt.html |work=The New York Times |page=1 |date=November 19, 1964 |access-date=2019-11-18 |archive-date=2021-05-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502133513/https://www.nytimes.com/1964/11/19/archives/italy-expels-2-egyptian-envoys-accused-in-trunk-abduction-attempt.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=ISP>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=es9Sunv_y2MC&q=Dikko+incident&pg=PA128 |title=''Islamic State Practices, International Law and the Threat from Terrorism'' |author=Javaid Rehman |date=7 June 2005 |publisher=Hart Publishing |isbn=9781841135014 |access-date=2008-10-05 |archive-date=2021-11-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211113174004/https://books.google.com/books?id=es9Sunv_y2MC&q=Dikko+incident&pg=PA128 |url-status=live }}</ref> The box that he had been sealed into "had almost certainly been used before for human cargo,"<ref>{{cite web|title=Kidnapped by Egypt: The Spy In The Air Express Trunk—It's Fact, Not Fiction—And It Has Happened Before|url=http://pgnewspapers.pgpl.ca/fedora/repository/pgc:1964-11-18/-/Prince%20George%20Citizen%20-%20November%2018,%201964|work=Prince George (B.C.) Citizen (p. 1)|date=November 18, 1964|access-date=2017-04-19|archive-date=2017-04-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170420054119/http://pgnewspapers.pgpl.ca/fedora/repository/pgc:1964-11-18/-/Prince%20George%20Citizen%20-%20November%2018,%201964|url-status=live}}</ref> including possibly for an Egyptian military official who had defected to Italy several years before but then disappeared without a trace before reappearing under Egyptian custody and facing trial.
* The Canadian government sent Canadian passports and other material via a diplomatic bag to [[Tehran]] to assist in the [[Canadian Caper|exfiltration of six American diplomats]] who had evaded capture during the [[Iran hostage crisis|seizure of the United States embassy.]]
* During the 1982 [[Falklands War]], the Argentine government used a diplomatic bag to smuggle several [[limpet mine]]s to their embassy in Spain, to be used in the covert [[Operation Algeciras]], in which Argentine agents were to blow up a British warship in the [[Royal Navy Dockyard]] at [[Gibraltar]]. The plot was uncovered and stopped by the Spanish police before the explosives could be set.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chronicle.gi/headlines_details.php?id=27328 |title=Argentina's 1982 attempt on Gibraltar |publisher=Gibraltar Chronicle |date=December 28, 2012 |access-date=December 1, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203011748/http://www.chronicle.gi/headlines_details.php?id=27328 |archive-date=December 3, 2013 }}</ref>
* In the 1984 [[Dikko Affair]], a former [[Nigeria]]n government minister, [[Umaru Dikko]], was kidnapped and placed in a shipping crate in an attempt to transport him from the United Kingdom back to Nigeria for trial.<ref name=ISP/> However, it was not marked as a diplomatic bag, which allowed British customs to open it.<ref name=ISP/> 
* In 1984, the [[Sterling submachine gun]] used to kill [[Police ranks of the United Kingdom#History of police ranks|WPC]] [[Murder of Yvonne Fletcher|Yvonne Fletcher]] from inside the [[Libya]]n Embassy in London was smuggled out of the [[UK]] in one of 21 diplomatic bags.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/africaandindianocean/libya/6345907/Yvonne-Fletcher-Libya-and-betrayal-of-justice-timeline.html | location=London | work=The Daily Telegraph | url-status=live }}<br/>{{cite news | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/terrorism-in-the-uk/6341458/WPc-Yvonne-Fletcher-We-have-guns-and-there-will-be-fighting.html | location=London | |website=api.parliament.uk|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020182619/http://hansard.millbanksystems.com/commons/1984/may/15/searching-of-diplomatic-bags |archive-date=2012-10-20 }}<br/>{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/april/27/newsid_2502000/2502565.stm | work=BBC News | title=1984: Libyan embassy siege ends | date=1984-04-27 | url-status=live }}</ref>
* In March 2000, [[Zimbabwe]] became the object of international political attention when it opened a British diplomatic shipment.<ref name=BBC/>
* In May 2008, a replacement pump for the [[space toilet|toilet]] on the [[International Space Station]] was sent in a diplomatic pouch from Russia to the United States to arrive before liftoff of the next shuttle mission.<ref>{{cite web
 | url = http://www.redorbit.com/news/space/1407194/space_station_toilet_parts_set_for_liftoff 
 | url-status = dead
 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121001090819/http://www.redorbit.com/news/space/1407194/space_station_toilet_parts_set_for_liftoff/
 | archive-date = 2012-10-01
 | title = Space Station Toilet Parts Set for Liftoff}}</ref>
* In 2012, a {{convert|16|kg|lb|adj=on}} shipment of cocaine was sent to the United Nations in New York in a bag disguised as a diplomatic pouch.<ref>Associated Press, [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/jan/27/cocaine-seized-un-new-york Cocaine seized at UN in New York] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160314120146/http://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/jan/27/cocaine-seized-un-new-york |date=2016-03-14 }}, 26 January 2012</ref>
* In January 2012, Italy detected {{convert|40|kg}} of cocaine smuggled in a diplomatic pouch from Ecuador, arresting five. Ecuador insisted it had inspected the shipment for drugs at the foreign ministry before it was sent to Milan.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.starpoly.com/comunicado/ |title=Comunicado No. 012 |language=es |publisher=StarPoly |access-date=2014-05-06 |archive-date=2014-05-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140506220811/http://www.starpoly.com/comunicado/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
*In November 2013, the [[United Kingdom|UK]] government alleged that a British diplomatic bag had been opened by the [[Guardia Civil]] at the [[Disputed status of Gibraltar|Gibraltar-Spanish border]], sparking a formal diplomatic protest.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-25100083|work=BBC News|title=UK protest at Gibraltar diplomatic bag opening|date=2013-11-26|access-date=2018-06-20|archive-date=2018-05-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180501054509/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-25100083|url-status=live}}</ref> The Spanish government responded that the bag, being transported from the [[Governor of Gibraltar]] by a courier company, and contained in a mailbag that held other packages, did not meet the criteria of being in transit between a diplomatic mission and a home government.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/gibraltar/10477856/Spain-dismisses-Gibraltar-diplomatic-bag-incident.html |title=Spain dismisses Gibraltar diplomatic bag incident |author=Fiona Govan |newspaper=Daily Telegraph |date=27 November 2013 |access-date=4 December 2013 |archive-date=30 November 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131130100556/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/europe/gibraltar/10477856/Spain-dismisses-Gibraltar-diplomatic-bag-incident.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20131126/reino-unido-protesta-ante-espana-apertura-valija-diplomatica-gibraltar/802621.shtml |title=El Reino Unido ha protestado ante España l RTVE.es |language=es |date=November 26, 2013 |website=RTVE.es |access-date=December 24, 2021 |archive-date=September 18, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918141834/https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20131126/reino-unido-protesta-ante-espana-apertura-valija-diplomatica-gibraltar/802621.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>
* In July 2020, Indian officials detected {{convert|30|kg}} of gold smuggled in a concealed diplomatic consignment from the [[United Arab Emirates]], which was [[2020 Kerala gold smuggling case|seized at Thiruvananthapuram Airport]] in [[Kerala]] by the Indian Customs Department. India's [[National Investigation Agency]] revealed that former local UAE consulate employees were involved in gold smuggling.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/india/former-uae-consulate-employee-swapna-suresh-involved-in-kerala-gold-smuggling-prosecutor-1.1594382741176/ |title=Former UAE consulate employee Swapna Suresh involved in Kerala gold smuggling: prosecutor |date=July 10, 2020 |access-date=2020-07-12 |archive-date=2020-07-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200713000103/https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/india/former-uae-consulate-employee-swapna-suresh-involved-in-kerala-gold-smuggling-prosecutor-1.1594382741176 |url-status=live }}</ref>
